summary: caffeine amount in 1 portion is what the Coffee calculator works out, and it gets there from the body weight and the total caffeine. Think of it as a shortcut for portioning, timing or nutrition. Change one value and the results step aside until you press Calculate again, which is what makes it easy to see how much the answer really depends on that one input.

sections.title: How does the Coffee calculator work?
sections.html:
The Coffee calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports caffeine amount in 1 portion in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (your coffee sensitivity and the drink); then you type in the body weight and the total caffeine.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A measured quantity, entered by default in kilograms. The unit chip switches it to any of the 29 supported units.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 5 options, such as very tolerant, tolerant and average. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 178 options, such as 7 Eleven Brewed Coffee, alpine Start Instant Coffee and americano Coffee. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A number, expressed in mg.

2 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Coffee calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Caffeine amount in 1 portion=your coffee sensitivity × body weight ÷ number of portions
Caffeine amount in 1 portion=total caffeine ÷ number of portions

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Take Body weight = 10 kg, Your coffee sensitivity set to Average, Drink set to 7 Eleven Brewed Coffee and Number of portions = 10. The calculator returns Total caffeine = 100.

The point of the example is the scale, not the particular digits: swap in your own figures and the same relationship produces your answer.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Total caffeine = 100 should be roughly the size you expected from Body weight = 10 kg and Your coffee sensitivity set to Average.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:

  • A number, filled in as soon as the inputs allow it.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Mass, opening in kilograms

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Coffee calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Working out timing so everything finishes together
  • Scaling a recipe up or down
  • Checking portions before you shop
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the body weight and the total caffeine — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Coffee calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns caffeine amount in 1 portion, derived from the body weight and the total caffeine. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Coffee calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the body weight and the total caffeine, which is 4 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter body weight in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Body weight opens in kilograms and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Total caffeine = 100. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Coffee calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
